 Bears report: TE Colston Loveland good to go vs. Seahawks despite neck injury
 Plus, Theo Benedet will start again at left tackle and more.
 By  
 Jason Lieser 
 [month] [day], [year], [hour]:[minute][ampm] [timezone] 
 Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland (84) catches a pass against the Atlanta Falcons during the second half of an NFL football game in Atlanta, Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026. (AP Photo/Mike Stewart) ORG XMIT: TNMH131
 Mike Stewart/AP Photos

 What happened Saturday at Halas Hall:
 Loveland doing fine 
 Tight end Colston Loveland was back at practice after missing time Friday because of what he called a ‘‘little tweak’’ in his neck suffered while lifting weights. He will play Monday against the Seahawks and said: ‘‘I’m good. I don’t even know why it’s a thing.’’
 Benedet sticks 
 Theo Benedet is playing well enough at left tackle to keep Ozzy Trapilo on a limited workload, and coach Ben Johnson said Benedet will make his fifth consecutive start.
 Trapilo was a second-round pick in 2025 and took over the starting job last November, but the Bears are taking it slowly with him coming off a knee injury. He has played 36 snaps on offensive and 13 on special teams in the last two games.
 Controversial footwear 
 As fines escalate for quarterback Caleb Williams wearing Caddix cleats , the NFL could bar him from playing in them unless he covers the logo. Section 4 of the rulebook allows that enforcement, but Johnson said he was confident Williams would find a way to avoid any issues. He wore all-white Caddix cleats in the first two games and wasn’t penalized.
 Monangai delayed 
 The Bears didn’t put running back Kyle Monangai on injured reserve after he hurt his toe Oct. 4, but he’ll miss his fourth game anyway. Johnson couldn’t say whether he’s progressing toward returning next week against the Buccaneers.
 Green light 
 Seahawks running backs Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet were cleared from their injuries and are expected to play.
